However, to date, the said application has not been processed by CEA on account of the pendency of W.P. (C) No. 838 of 2019 titled “M.K. Ranjitsinh & Ors. v. Union of India” (“GIB Writ Petition”) before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, which has been reserved for Judgment on 29.11.2025. _**“** The matter, along with the IA, was mentioned by the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, citing the urgency therein._ _3. Considering the submissions made by the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed that notice be issued to the Respondent to file its reply within a week, with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file a rejoinder thereof within two days thereafter.”_ _(g) CTUIL ought to be restrained from taking any coercive steps, including the creation of third-party rights in relation to the Petitioner's connectivity, till the disposal of the Petition._ _4. Further, at the request of the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission permitted the Respondent, CTUIL, to file its note of submissions within a week, with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its note of submissions within a week thereafter. The Commission also directed that the quantum corresponding to the Petitioner's connectivity at Bhadla III PS shall not be reallocated to any other developers till the outcome of the Petition._ _(a) A copy of the amendment (if any) to the final grant of connectivity to the Petitioner._ _(b) When did CTUIL confirm the firm start of connectivity to the Petitioner and the necessary proof thereof?_ ## **Petitioner’s Submission in Compliance with the RoP for the hearing dated 08.01.2026** 12. The Petitioner, in its submissions dated 12.02.2026, in response to the note dated 08.01.2026, additional note dated 03.02.2026 and RoP compliance affidavit dated 03.02.2026 by CTUIL, submitted as under: 20. We have considered the submissions of Petitioner and Respondent. The following As per the above, the Petitioner submitted an undertaking, the Principal Loan Sanction Letter, net-worth and Board resolution for equity commitment. The snapshot of the documents submitted by the Petitioner is as under: As per the above, the Petitioner submitted the above six documents, including the Board Resolutions dated 25[th] November 2025 and undertaking dated 27.11.2025. 43. We do not agree with the petitioner’s contention that it furnished a Board resolution on 28.8.2025, which should have been considered by CTUIL for meeting Financial Closure, as we have already noted that the petitioner had itself furnished an undertaking dated 28.8.2025 for project funding mainly through a loan; therefore, it cannot argue that it was funding the entire project through equity on 28.8.2025. 44. Petitioner has argued that CTU itself belatedly pointed out a discrepancy in its inprinciple sanction letter, and Petitioner furnished revised documents – revised Board resolution and revised undertaking within 10 days of pointing out this discrepancy by CTU, and hence should not be penalised by revocation of Connectivity. _“27._ _**We have considered the submissions of Petitioners and the information on record. As per the submission of the Petitioners, they have achieved the financial closure within the stipulated time i.e. on 21.06.2025 against the last date of 25.06.2025 in case of 768/MP/2025 and on 23.06.2025 against the last date of 26.06.2025 in case of 769/MP/2025, but have failed in timely submission of documents and submitted it after delay of 54 and 56 days respectively.**_ _32. Accordingly, we condone the delay in furnishing proof/ copy of financial closure documents in terms of the first proviso to Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA 2nd Amendment Regulations 2024 by the petitioners, subject to payment of compensation equivalent to 5% of the total Conn BGs amount submitted by the petitioners within 15 days of this Order. The amount received by the CTUIL under the aforementioned compensation shall be utilised to reduce the monthly transmission charges under the 2020 Sharing Regulations. On receipt of the compensation amount from the petitioners, CTUIL is directed to reinstate/ restore the connectivity of the Petitioners. However, this order shall not be treated as a precedent, having been decided keeping in view the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.”_
title: Petition under Sections 79(1)(c), 79(1)(f) and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access) Regulations, 2022 (as amended) and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business Regulations), 2023, seeking directions to Central Transmission Utility of India Limited to consider the documents furnished by Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited as compliance of the Financial Closure requirement under Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations, 2022 (as amended) or, in the alternative, to communicate the firm start date of Connectivity and grant a period of 06 (six) months prior thereto for achieving Financial Closure. Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited
